newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Ebro sees merger with Azucarera delayed.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Ebro sees merger with Azucarera delayed.

text.p: The planned merger between Spanish sugar producers Ebro de Agricolas and Azucarera will be delayed by a parliamentary proposal from the governing Popular Party (PP), sources at Ebro said on Friday.
Stock market watchdog CNMV said late Thursday the Popular Party had issued a proposal which sets out reasons the PP considered valid for the merger to be postponed.
The PP statement said it would like the final structure of the new group to "guarantee the company's future (within) Agro-industrial activity and its Spanish nature".
This conflicts with demands by France's Saint-Louis's Generale Sucriere, a stakeholder in both companies, to control the new group.
PP also asked the government, before the possible merger, to push for an increased Spanish sugar quota.
Sources at Ebro said the parliamentary discussion could take time.
"This is a decision which has to be made by politicians, whether they would like to delay (the merger)...It's a (parliamentary) process that could take some months," the source said.
The two Spanish companies started talks on a possible merger in December last year.
